The test image shows a ripe tomato fruit with dark, sunken, circular lesions showing concentric rings and dark gray/black fungal sporulation. This pattern is classic for fruit rot diseases. Top candidates: **Anthracnose** (sunken circular lesions with sporulation), **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**, **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**.

Let me view references one at a time across different classes.

Excellent match! Anthracnose Bugwood_17 shows a ripe red tomato with a large circular, sunken lesion with concentric rings — very similar to the test image. Let me check one more class before concluding.

Phytophthora blight shows wilted blackened stems — completely different from the test image.

**Summary of visual analysis:**

- **Test image**: Ripe orange/red tomato fruit with circular, sunken lesions showing concentric rings and dark gray/black sporulation. Multiple lesions visible.
- **Anthracnose (Bugwood_17)**: Ripe red tomato with large circular, sunken lesion with concentric rings and dark acervuli — **strong visual match**.
- **Alternaria/Stem Cankers**: Shows stem canker on seedlings — wrong plant part.
- **Rhizopus Soft Rots**: Shows fluffy white mycelium with black sporangia — different appearance.
- **Gray Mold**: Shows cracked, decayed gray-fuzzy growth at stem end — different pattern.
- **Phytophthora Blight**: Shows wilted blackened stems — different.

The circular, sunken, concentric-ring lesions with dark sporulation on ripe tomato fruit is the hallmark presentation of **Anthracnose** (Colletotrichum spp.).
